title: University of Cambridge PhD Applications 2027/28
content:
The University of Cambridge offers some of the most prestigious fully funded opportunities for international students to pursue a PhD. The two primary funding routes for Nigerian, African, and international applicants are the Gates Cambridge Scholarship and the Cambridge Trust awards. Navigating these applications requires careful planning, as the funding deadlines are strict and highly competitive.

Last checked: October 2026

Current 2027 Application Status

Applications for the 2027/28 academic year at the University of Cambridge are currently open. To be considered for funding, including the Gates Cambridge Scholarship and the Cambridge Trust, you must apply by the specific funding deadline for your course.

Quick Facts

Opportunity Institution Country Study Level Status Deadline Funding Eligible Applicants
Gates Cambridge / Cambridge Trust University of Cambridge United Kingdom PhD Open 14 Oct 2026 (US Residents) / 8 Dec 2026 or 6 Jan 2027 (International) Full tuition, stipend, travel International Students

Funding Details

According to the university, both the Gates Cambridge Scholarship and the Cambridge Trust awards are comprehensive. The funding typically includes:

  • University Composition Fee: Full coverage of tuition fees at the appropriate rate.
  • Maintenance Allowance: A generous stipend for a single student to cover living costs.
  • Travel Costs: One economy single airfare at both the beginning and end of the course.
  • Visa Costs: Inbound visa costs and the cost of the Immigration Health Surcharge.

CEE recommends factoring in additional personal expenses, as the stipend is designed for a single student. If you plan to bring dependents, you will need to demonstrate additional independent funding.

Application Advice and Requirements

According to the university, applicants must demonstrate outstanding intellectual ability, reasons for the choice of course, and a commitment to improving the lives of others (specifically for Gates Cambridge). You must also secure a potential supervisor before applying.

CEE recommends contacting potential supervisors at least two to three months before the funding deadline. Crafting a compelling research proposal and securing strong letters of recommendation are critical to your success. If you need assistance structuring your proposal or polishing your personal statement, our experts at CEE Writing Services are available to help you stand out.

Application Checklist

  • Identify a potential supervisor and secure their initial support.
  • Draft and refine your research proposal.
  • Prepare your personal statement (and the Gates Cambridge reference, if applicable).
  • Request academic and personal references early.
  • Complete the University of Cambridge Graduate Application Portal.
  • Submit by the course funding deadline (typically 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 for international applicants).

title: Imperial College London PhD Applications 2027
content:
Imperial College London offers one of the most prestigious funding opportunities for international students: the President's PhD Scholarships. This guide breaks down everything you need to know to submit a strong application for the 2027 entry cycle, tailored specifically for high-achieving applicants from Africa and around the world.

Last checked: October 2026

Current 2027 Application Status

Applications for the 2026/2027 cycle (for a 2027 start) are currently Open. The selection process takes place over three rounds throughout the academic year. It is highly recommended to apply as early as possible, as supervisors are limited to supporting only one applicant per cycle.

Quick Facts

Feature Details
Opportunity President's PhD Scholarships
Institution Imperial College London
Country United Kingdom
Study level PhD
Status Open
Deadline Round 1: Nov 2, 2026 | Round 2: Jan 11, 2027 | Round 3: Mar 1, 2027
Funding Full tuition, stipend, and consumables fund
Eligible applicants All nationalities (No restrictions)

Detailed Funding Breakdown

When applying for this scholarship, it is important to understand exactly what is covered. This is a comprehensive package:

  • Full Tuition Fees: Your overseas tuition fees will be fully covered for up to 3.5 years.
  • Living Stipend: An annual tax-free living stipend at the UKRI rate plus a London weighting (typically enough to comfortably cover housing and living expenses in London) for up to 3.5 years.
  • Consumables Fund: An allowance of £2,000 per year for the first 3 years to cover research materials, equipment, and conference travel.

Official Requirements vs. Expert Advice

To maximize your chances, you must balance the university's baseline requirements with what actually makes an applicant stand out.

Academic Excellence

  • According to the university: You must have, or be on track to receive, a First Class UK undergraduate degree (or equivalent). If you have a Master's, it must be awarded with a Distinction.
  • CEE recommends: For international candidates, especially from Nigeria and other African countries, your transcript should clearly demonstrate top percentile performance. Emphasize any awards, publications, or significant research projects in your CV to contextualize your academic excellence globally.

Supervisory Support

  • According to the university: You must have contacted a supervisor who has agreed to support your application before you apply.
  • CEE recommends: Supervisors are highly selective because they can only support one candidate per cycle. Do not send generic emails. Read their recent publications and draft a highly tailored research proposal summary when reaching out. If you need help refining your academic outreach, consider utilizing CEE Writing Services to polish your proposal and introductory emails.

Application Checklist

Ensure you have completed all of the following steps before submitting your application:

  • Identify a potential academic supervisor at Imperial College London.
  • Reach out and secure their formal agreement to support your application.
  • Prepare your Statement of Purpose (Personal Statement) detailing your research interests and motivation.
  • Finalize a concise, structured research proposal (in collaboration with your prospective supervisor).
  • Gather all academic transcripts and degree certificates.
  • Select two strong academic referees (one must be your current or most recent academic supervisor).
  • Submit the standard Imperial College London PhD application online.
  • In the funding section of the application, explicitly select the option to be considered for the President's PhD Scholarships.

Applying for the President's PhD Scholarships requires significant preparation, but the reward is one of the most generous funding packages in the UK. Start early, communicate effectively with potential supervisors, and present a flawless application.

title: Carleton University PhD Applications 2027
content:
Welcome to our comprehensive guide for applying to PhD programs at Carleton University for the 2026/2027 academic cycle (starting in Fall 2027). Securing a PhD position with full funding in Canada is a rigorous process, but with the right preparation and understanding of the requirements, international students can build highly competitive applications.

Last checked: October 2026

Current 2027 Application Status

The application cycle for the Fall 2027 intake at Carleton University is currently gearing up. According to the university, application deadlines are program-specific. Some programs have cutoff dates as early as January 2027 for the Fall 2027 start, while others operate on a rolling basis. International students are strongly encouraged by Carleton University to complete applications at least five to six months before their intended start date. CEE recommends applying even earlier, well before the first program deadline, to ensure guaranteed consideration for standard graduate funding packages.

Quick Facts

Opportunity Institution Country Study Level Status Deadline Funding Eligible Applicants
PhD Programs (Various Fields) Carleton University Canada Doctorate (PhD) Opening Soon Varies by program (e.g., Jan-Mar 2027) Funded (TA/RA standard packages) Domestic & International Students

Understanding Funding at Carleton University

Funding is a critical component of your PhD application. According to the university, when you apply for admission, you are automatically considered for funding; there is no separate application required for standard graduate funding packages. This standard package typically includes:

  • Teaching Assistantships (TAs): Paid positions assisting with undergraduate courses.
  • Research Assistantships (RAs): Paid research work typically funded by your supervisor's research grants.
  • Scholarships and Bursaries: Merit-based internal awards provided by the university or department.

CEE advises that while standard packages cover significant costs, you should carefully review the specific funding offer upon admission, as living expenses in Ottawa and international tuition fees will need to be met. Additionally, CEE recommends applying for external funding (like OGS or Vanier CGS) if eligible, though these often have earlier deadlines.

Application Checklist

Before submitting your application, ensure you have prepared the following components. If you need professional support in crafting a compelling statement of purpose or academic CV, CEE Writing Services can help you refine your application materials to meet Canadian university standards.

  • Check the specific graduate program deadline on the Carleton University Graduate Admissions website.
  • Secure a thesis supervisor (required by most PhD programs prior to application).
  • Prepare your Statement of Intent or Research Proposal.
  • Update your Academic CV highlighting research experience and publications.
  • Gather all official transcripts from previous post-secondary institutions.
  • Arrange for 2-3 academic reference letters (referees will be contacted directly).
  • Verify and meet English language proficiency requirements (IELTS, TOEFL, etc.).
  • Ensure all materials are submitted well ahead of the "guaranteed consideration" deadline for funding.

title: NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship 2027–28
content:
The NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Program provides funding to PhD students who are researching topics that will lead to major advances in the graphics, AI, and high-performance computing industries. As one of the most prestigious industry fellowships available to computing and artificial intelligence researchers, it offers exceptional financial support and direct integration with NVIDIA's cutting-edge research teams.

Last verified / updated: October 2026

Current 2027 Application Status

The application period for the 2027–2028 academic year is currently open. Applications must be submitted by October 30, 2026. Late submissions will not be considered. Given the rigorous selection process and the need for recommendation letters, CEE recommends completing your application materials well ahead of this deadline.

Quick Facts

Opportunity Institution / Sponsor Country Study Level Status Deadline Funding Eligible Applicants
NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship NVIDIA Global (must be enrolled in a recognized university) PhD Open October 30, 2026 Up to $60,000 Active PhD students (post-1st year)

Funding Details

According to the official NVIDIA fellowship guidelines, recipients receive an award of up to $60,000 to support their PhD research. It is important to note how this funding is structured:

  • Grant Amount: Up to $60,000 for the nine-month academic year (2027-2028). This can generally be used to cover living expenses, tuition, or research costs.
  • Internship: A mandatory paid in-person summer internship at an NVIDIA research office prior to the fellowship year (Summer 2027). This provides both additional income and invaluable industry experience.

CEE advises applicants to consult their university's financial aid or graduate studies office, as some institutions may have specific policies on how external grants like this interact with existing graduate funding packages or stipends.

Eligibility Requirements

According to the official program rules, applicants must meet the following criteria:

  • Must have completed at least the first year of PhD-level studies at the time of application.
  • Must be a full-time, active PhD student throughout the nine-month award year.
  • Must be engaged in active research related to areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, autonomous vehicles, computer graphics, healthcare, or high-performance computing.
  • Must be available for the mandatory summer 2027 internship at NVIDIA.

Application Checklist

Ensure you have prepared the following documents for your submission. If you need assistance structuring your proposal or refining your CV to meet industry standards, consider utilizing CEE Writing Services to help you present your research compellingly.

  • Research Proposal: Maximum 2 pages (plus bibliography). This should clearly outline your research goals, methodology, and how it aligns with NVIDIA's current research interests.
  • Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV): Highlighting your academic achievements, publications, and relevant technical experience.
  • Recommendation Letters: 2 to 3 letters of recommendation are required. Crucially, one of these letters must be from your official thesis advisor. Ensure you request these early through the NVIDIA research portal.

title: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Doctoral Scholarship 2027
content:
Last checked: October 2026

The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Doctoral Scholarship is one of Canada’s most prestigious and highly coveted awards for doctoral students in the humanities and social sciences. Designed to empower engaged leaders, the scholarship provides generous financial support and integrates scholars into an exceptional multidisciplinary network of mentors, fellows, and alumni. If your research tackles critical societal issues, this opportunity can accelerate both your academic career and your public impact.

Current 2027 Application Status

The application cycle for the 2027 cohort is currently open. Prospective applicants must meet the initial eligibility verification deadline of October 2, 2026, to proceed to the full application stage.

Quick Facts

Category Details
Opportunity Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Doctoral Scholarship
Institution Canadian universities (for international students/PRs) or any university (for Canadian citizens)
Country Canada (and abroad for Canadian citizens)
Study Level Doctoral (PhD) - Years 1 or 2
Status Open
Deadline November 6, 2026 (Eligibility form due October 2, 2026)
Funding Up to $50,000/year stipend + $20,000/year research allowance
Eligible Applicants Canadians, Permanent Residents, and International Students (at Canadian institutions)

Funding Details

According to the Foundation, the scholarship provides a comprehensive funding package for up to three years, totaling up to $210,000. It is critical to note how this funding is distributed:

  • Stipend: Up to $50,000 per year to cover tuition fees and living expenses. The Foundation guarantees a minimum annual stipend; however, the exact amount may be adjusted if the scholar holds other major external funding.
  • Research and Travel Allowance: Up to $20,000 per year specifically allocated for research, fieldwork, networking, and travel related to the doctoral project and Foundation-led leadership events.
  • Leadership Program: Scholars gain exclusive access to a three-year leadership program designed to nurture their skills in public engagement and translating research into action.

Eligibility Requirements

To be eligible for the 2027 scholarship cycle, applicants must meet specific criteria:

  • Academic Standing: You must be in your first or second year of a full-time doctoral program.
  • Citizenship and Affiliation:
    • International students and Canadian Permanent Residents must be enrolled in a full-time doctoral program at a Canadian university.
    • Canadian citizens can be enrolled at a Canadian university or a foreign university.
  • Field of Study: Your research must be within the humanities or social sciences.
  • Thematic Alignment: Your project must align with at least one of the Foundation’s four core themes: Human Rights and Dignity, Responsible Citizenship, Canada and the World, or People and their Natural Environment.

Application Checklist & Important Deadlines

CEE recommends marking these exact dates in your calendar. Missing the initial eligibility step will permanently disqualify you from the 2027 cycle.

  • October 2, 2026: Submit the mandatory eligibility verification form.
  • October 5 – October 12, 2026: Attend the mandatory information sessions (for verified eligible candidates).
  • October 30, 2026 (9:00 a.m. ET): Deadline for your three referees to submit their recommendation letters. CEE advises reminding your referees at least two weeks before this date.
  • November 6, 2026 (4:00 p.m. ET): Final deadline to submit the complete online application package, including transcripts and research proposals.

How CEE Writing Services Can Help

The Trudeau Foundation Scholarship is highly competitive and prioritizes students who can articulate the broader societal impact of their research. At CEE Writing Services, we specialize in helping international and African students frame their academic achievements into compelling narratives. Whether you need assistance brainstorming your public engagement strategy or require a thorough review of your research proposal, our experts can guide you through the intricacies of the Trudeau Scholarship application.

title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarship 2027/28
content:
The Commonwealth PhD Scholarship is one of the most prestigious fully funded opportunities for students from eligible Commonwealth countries to pursue doctoral studies in the United Kingdom. Designed to support future innovators, leaders, and researchers, this scholarship empowers individuals to contribute to the development of their home countries while gaining world-class academic experience.

Last checked: October 2026

Current 2027 Application Status

The application window for the 2027/2028 academic year is currently open. Applications must be submitted through the official CSC Central electronic application system. It is strongly recommended to prepare all required documents well in advance to avoid last-minute technical difficulties.

Quick Facts

Category Details
Opportunity Commonwealth PhD Scholarship 2027/28
Institution Various UK Universities
Country United Kingdom
Study Level PhD (Doctoral degree)
Status Open
Deadline 20 October 2026 at 16:00 BST (CSC Portal)
Funding Fully Funded (Tuition, Stipend, Airfare, Allowances)
Eligible Applicants Citizens of eligible Commonwealth countries

Funding Details

The Commonwealth PhD Scholarship is exceptionally generous and covers all essential expenses for your doctoral study. According to the official provisions, the scholarship includes:

  • Full Tuition Fees: Complete coverage of all approved university tuition fees.
  • Living Stipend: A regular monthly living allowance to cover accommodation and daily expenses.
  • Travel Costs: Approved airfare from your home country to the UK at the start of your award, and a return flight at the end.
  • Additional Allowances: A warm clothing allowance upon arrival, a study travel grant towards the cost of study-related travel within the UK or overseas, and, in some cases, family allowances for eligible scholars.

Eligibility and Application Requirements

To be considered for the Commonwealth PhD Scholarship, applicants must meet several strict criteria. According to the CSC, you must:

  • Be a citizen of or have been granted refugee status by an eligible Commonwealth country.
  • Be permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country.
  • Be available to start your academic studies in the UK by September/October 2027.
  • Hold a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours standard, or a second-class degree and a relevant postgraduate qualification (usually a Master’s degree).

CEE recommends: Beyond the basic requirements, your research proposal is the most critical part of your application. The CSC focuses heavily on the development impact of your research. Ensure your proposal clearly demonstrates how your work will benefit your home country. If you need assistance structuring your proposal or polishing your essays, our CEE Writing Services can help you stand out to the nominating agencies.

Application Checklist

Ensure you have the following documents ready before submitting your application to the CSC portal and your national nominating agency:

  • Proof of citizenship or refugee status (e.g., passport).
  • Full academic transcripts and degree certificates (undergraduate and postgraduate).
  • At least two compelling letters of recommendation.
  • A well-structured research proposal demonstrating development impact.
  • Supporting statement from a proposed supervisor at a UK university (if required by your scheme).

Please note that many national nominating agencies have their own internal deadlines that fall significantly earlier than the CSC deadline of 20 October 2026. Always verify the specific internal deadline with your nominating body.

title: AfricaLics PhD Visiting Fellowship 2027
content:
The AfricaLics PhD Visiting Fellowship Programme (VFP) provides an exceptional opportunity for African PhD students working in the field of Innovation and Development to spend three months at the University of Johannesburg, South Africa. This fellowship is designed to support scholars by providing dedicated time, mentorship, and training to advance their doctoral research. It is important to note that this is a visiting fellowship for current PhD students, not a full PhD admission scholarship.

Last checked: October 2026

Current 2027 Application Status

The application cycle for the 2027 AfricaLics PhD Visiting Fellowship is currently open. The application deadline is October 2, 2026. The fellowship includes online pre- and post-activities starting in February 2027 and a physical residency at the University of Johannesburg scheduled from September 6 to December 3, 2027.

Quick Facts

Opportunity Institution Country Study Level Status Deadline Funding Eligible Applicants
AfricaLics PhD Visiting Fellowship 2027 University of Johannesburg South Africa (Residency) PhD (Current students) Open October 2, 2026 Fully funded study visit (travel, accommodation, stipend) African PhD students in low/lower-middle-income countries

Funding Details

According to the official fellowship guidelines, the AfricaLics VFP provides comprehensive support for the 3-month residential study visit. The funding covers:

  • Travel: Return economy-class airfare from your nearest international airport to Johannesburg.
  • Accommodation: Fully covered for the duration of the 3-month stay.
  • Stipend: A monthly stipend of approximately US$600 to cover living expenses and local travel in Johannesburg.
  • Training & Mentorship: Costs for participation in joint courses and mentorship fees.
  • Insurance: Travel insurance (serving as basic health insurance) is provided.
  • Additional Support: Limited funds are available for participation in relevant short courses not available in the student's home country.

CEE recommends: Remember that this fellowship does not fund your basic PhD tuition or research costs at your home institution. You are expected to have secured your primary PhD funding from other sources. Treat this stipend as living support during your 3-month stay in South Africa, and ensure you budget accordingly.

Eligibility and Official Requirements

According to the university and AfricaLics guidelines, applicants must meet the following criteria:

  • Be currently enrolled as a PhD student at an African university.
  • Have a research focus related to Innovation and Development (I&D).
  • Be a citizen of an African country classified by the OECD/DAC as low-income or lower-middle-income.
  • Have completed your first year of PhD studies by December 2026.

Female students and candidates from low-income countries are highly encouraged to apply.

Application Checklist

To prepare a strong application, ensure you have the following documents ready before the deadline:

  • A brief outline of your current PhD project (including research objectives, methodology, and progress).
  • A motivation letter explaining why the AfricaLics Visiting Fellowship will benefit your PhD research and career in Innovation and Development.
  • Your updated Curriculum Vitae (CV).
  • A letter of support from your primary PhD supervisor at your home university.
  • Proof of current PhD registration.

CEE advice: A compelling motivation letter is crucial for a fellowship like this. Your letter must clearly demonstrate how access to the University of Johannesburg's resources and the AfricaLics network will directly impact your research outcomes. If you need assistance in structuring your motivation letter or refining your research outline, consider utilizing our academic writing and review services to maximize your chances of success.
